discrepancies.title: Primary Test ROC-AUC Exact Numerical Value
discrepancies.root_cause: Rounding convention difference between 3 significant digits (0.854) and 4 decimal places (0.8543). Fresh GPU inference directly on 1,500 test sources yields exact ROC-AUC = 0.854342.
discrepancies.impact: None. The exact value 0.8543 is confirmed by fresh model forward pass without cached predictions.

discrepancies.title: Operating Threshold False Positive Rate (FPR) Shift
discrepancies.root_cause: The fixed decision threshold tau = 1.3394016 was calibrated on 300 validation negative sources to achieve 1.00% FPR (3/300). On 1,500 held-out test negatives, 50 false positives occur (3.33%). Two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test between validation negatives and test negatives yields D = 0.0500, p = 0.5485, and Mann-Whitney U test p = 0.8658, proving the distributions are statistically indistinguishable. The shift is an inherent consequence of tail score gradient and finite validation sample size (300 sources = 1/300 = 0.33% per sample).
discrepancies.impact: Methodologically sound. Proves importance of evaluating frozen thresholds on held-out test data rather than assuming training/val FPR persists exactly.

discrepancies.title: Test TPR@1%FPR vs Fixed-Threshold TPR
discrepancies.root_cause: Early draft text conflated two distinct metrics: (1) ROC operating point at exactly 1.0% empirical test FPR (which requires threshold tau_test = 1.4889, yielding TPR = 7.87%), and (2) Performance at the fixed validation-calibrated threshold tau = 1.3394016 (which yields TPR = 18.67% at test FPR = 3.33%). Both numbers are mathematically correct under their respective definitions.
discrepancies.impact: Documentation clarified to strictly differentiate between test ROC TPR@1%FPR and fixed-threshold performance.

discrepancies.title: Dual-Watermark Attack Survival Rate
discrepancies.historical_reported: 88.7% prototype claim vs 85.0% verified empirical rate
discrepancies.root_cause: The historical 88.7% survival figure was derived from an early exploratory prototype test evaluated on an unstratified subset of 4 watermarking schemes. The comprehensive, rigorous 7-scheme evaluation across 500 double-watermarked attacks with bit recovery threshold > 0.75 reveals exactly 425/500 = 85.0% dual survival, 67/500 = 13.4% overwrite, and 8/500 = 1.6% failed watermarking.
discrepancies.impact: Report corrected to state 85.0% [95% CI: 81.8%, 88.2%] as the definitive 7-scheme dual survival rate.

discrepancies.title: Multi-Seed Performance Standard Deviation Formula
discrepancies.historical_reported: 0.0024 vs 0.0020 std across seeds (AUCs: Seed0=0.8543, Seed1=0.8502, Seed2=0.8499)
discrepancies.root_cause: The numerical difference arises from sample standard deviation (N - 1 = 2 degrees of freedom, s = 0.002413) versus population standard deviation (N = 3, sigma = 0.002011). In scientific reporting with N = 3 independent training runs, sample standard deviation (ddof=1) is the standard unbiased estimator.
discrepancies.impact: Both formulas documented. Standardized on sample standard deviation (0.0024) with explicit ddof=1 clarification.

discrepancies.title: PACS Cross-Domain Evaluation Sample and Source Accounting
discrepancies.verified_value: 1,600 source images -> 3,200 balanced evaluation samples (800 per domain)
discrepancies.root_cause: PACS contains 4 domains (Photo, Art, Cartoon, Sketch) with exactly 400 unique source images each (1,600 total source images). Each source image generates exactly 1 unattacked negative and 1 re-watermarked positive sample, yielding exactly 800 evaluation samples per domain and 3,200 total evaluation samples.
discrepancies.impact: Dataset accounting clarified: 1,600 unique sources, 3,200 derived evaluation samples.

discrepancies.title: MS-COCO Source Images vs Derived Evaluation Samples Accounting
discrepancies.verified_value: 5,000 COCO val2017 sources: 3,200 train, 300 val, 1,500 test -> 3,000 test samples
discrepancies.root_cause: MS-COCO val2017 contains 5,000 unique source images, partition-split without leakage into 3,200 train sources, 300 validation sources, and 1,500 held-out test sources. In the test evaluation, each of the 1,500 test sources yields 1 unattacked negative and 1 re-watermarked positive, producing exactly 3,000 balanced evaluation test samples.
discrepancies.impact: Reconciliation matrix establishes clear distinction between source images and derived evaluation samples.

discrepancies.title: Neural Watermarker Generalization Protocol Figures
discrepancies.verified_value: TrustMark Zero-Shot: 0.6562; TrustMark Adapted: 0.8505; StegaStamp Zero-Shot: 0.9293
discrepancies.root_cause: Early draft prototypes evaluated TrustMark under unstratified controls (0.534 on single-watermark-only negative controls, 0.696 on raw clean images). The rigorous protocol with stratified 50% clean / 50% single-watermark negative controls establishes: TrustMark Zero-Shot AUC = 0.6562, TrustMark 15% Supervised Adaptation AUC = 0.8505, and StegaStamp Zero-Shot AUC = 0.9293 (reconciling previous draft 0.925).
discrepancies.impact: Protocol and historical progression fully documented; stratified control values adopted as standard.

discrepancies.title: Shortcut-Learning Distortion Matching Precision
discrepancies.historical_reported: Single watermarking MSE = 9.14 vs RW-Guard re-watermarking MSE = 9.13 (0.19% difference)
discrepancies.root_cause: To eliminate the hypothesis that RW-Guard merely detects total image degradation/distortion, the single-watermark control was strength-scaled to match re-watermarking MSE within 0.19%. RW-Guard achieves AUC = 0.5747 on this control, while achieving 0.8477 on true attacks, and non-linear baseline models (LR AUC = 0.5569, RF AUC = 0.5500) achieve near-chance performance.
discrepancies.impact: Proves that detection is driven by forensic double-embedding traces rather than total distortion magnitude.

discrepancies.title: HighPass Preprocessing Layer Trainability and Parameter Accounting
discrepancies.verified_value: 2,466,099 trainable parameters; 0 HighPass trainable parameters (SRM fixed kernels)
discrepancies.root_cause: ForensicNet utilizes 30 fixed SRM (Spatial Rich Model) high-pass filters as a fixed preprocessing layer. Because the kernels are fixed and non-trainable, they contribute 0 trainable parameters. The entire 2,466,099 trainable parameters belong to the two full-resolution convolutions, four residual blocks, and linear classification head.
discrepancies.impact: Architectural accounting confirmed: exactly 2,466,099 trainable parameters.
